_meta.method: DUAL-PATH DERIVATION (from 2026-07-24). Every expected value is produced by TWO independently written implementations that must agree to the cent: scripts/validate.py walks Artigo 68.º cumulatively on the marginal rates, scripts/oracle.py uses the taxa-média split the article itself publishes. A case the two paths disagree on is NOT written to this file — it is reported as a finding. Run `python scripts/oracle.py --crosscheck` to reproduce.
_meta.separate_filing_note: Cases 15-19 exercise tributação separada: each spouse is assessed INDIVIDUALLY (own rendimento coletável, quociente divisor 1, own coleta, own deduções à coleta with own global-cap limit on their own RC, own retenção) and the household figure is the SUM of the individual liquidações. Cases carrying a per_taxpayer expected block additionally verify the decomposition, not just the sum. Cases 15/16 and 17/18 are separada/conjunta twins on identical inputs so the euro delta is harness-derived, not asserted. Attribution conventions (household deductions split 50/50; case-level retention split pro-rata to gross) are documented in constants.json documented_approximations.
_meta.rounding: ROUND_HALF_UP to cents at coleta_bruta (after quociente multiply-back), each dedução, the global-cap limit, coleta_liquida, and apuramento.

conventions.apuramento: signed = retention_total - coleta_liquida. Positive = REEMBOLSO (refund). Negative = A_PAGAR (owed). Zero = NEUTRO.

_meta.law_version: Artigo 68.º na redação da Lei n.º 55-A/2025, de 22 de julho
_meta.method_history: Until 2026-07-24 this field read: 'Each case was hand-computed FIRST, then confirmed reproducible by scripts/validate.py --selftest. Expected values are NEVER edited to match code.' That protocol was sound against ENGINE regressions and useless against a wrong CONSTANT: the whole corpus was hand-derived by the author of the engine from the author's own reading of the law, so a shared mistake reproduced perfectly. It did exactly that for a year — the income-year-2025 bracket table carried the pre-Lei-55-A/2025 rates and all 19 cases agreed with it, 19/19 green. Worse, the 'never edit expected values' rule, applied literally when the rates were corrected, would have forced reverting the CORRECT fix, because the corpus carried no law-version stamp and so could not distinguish 'the engine broke' from 'the law changed'. Hence law_version below, and the dual-path rule above.
_meta.on_law_change: A bracket/cap change makes this corpus go red BY DESIGN. That red is not a regression. Procedure: (1) update the constant with its citation; (2) `oracle.py --crosscheck` must pass — it verifies the stored taxa-média column against the new marginal rates, which is the check that would have caught the 2025 defect; (3) `oracle.py --mutation-test` must pass; (4) `oracle.py --derive` regenerates expected values ONLY where both paths agree; (5) bump law_version. Never hand-edit an expected value to make a test green.
_meta.workings_note: On 2026-07-24 the Artigo 68.o rates were corrected to the Lei n.o 55-A/2025 table and every expected value was regenerated by oracle.py --derive. The hand-written `workings` prose was NOT regenerated, so 16 of 19 cases carried superseded arithmetic beside a correct answer for the length of that session - the exact 'stale prose next to correct code' failure this project warns about elsewhere. Those cases now carry `workings_historical` (explicitly labelled pre-correction) and every case carries `derivation_check`, which sweep.py asserts against expected[]. The check is what makes recurrence impossible; the relabelling alone would not.

cases.label: Tributação SEPARADA, two ~equal earners (20k/20k), household health split 50/50
cases.derivation: dual-path: scripts/validate.py (marginal-cumulative) and scripts/oracle.py (taxa-media split) agree to the cent
cases.workings_historical: [PRE-CORRECTION — computed on the superseded Artigo 68.o rates that Lei n.o 55-A/2025 replaced. Retained as the audit trail of the original hand-derivation; it does NOT describe the current expected values.] SEPARADA = two individual assessments, divisor 1 each, summed. Household deductions {health 2000} split 50/50 -> 1000 each. Retention 5000 split pro-rata to gross (equal gross) -> 2500 each. PER SPOUSE (both identical): net_A = 20000-4462.15 = 15537.85 = RC. Bracket 3 (12160-17233 @0.22). coleta = T(12160)+(15537.85-12160)*0.22 = 1724.335 + 3377.85*0.22 = 1724.335 + 743.127 = 2467.462 -> 2467.46. health ded = min(0.15*1000=150, 1000)=150; global limit at RC 15537.85 = 1000+1500*(83696-15537.85)/75637 = 2351.68 (non-binding, 150<2351.68). total_deducoes=150. coleta_liquida = 2467.46-150 = 2317.46. apuramento = 2500-2317.46 = 182.54 -> REEMBOLSO. COMBINED: coleta_liquida = 2*2317.46 = 4634.92; apuramento = 2*182.54 = 365.08 -> REEMBOLSO. WHY separada==conjunta here (see twin case 16, delta 0.00): both spouses share ONE bracket (3), where tax(x) is affine, so tax(a)+tax(b) = 2*tax((a+b)/2); and 0.15*1000*2 = 0.15*2000 with neither hitting the 1000 cap, so the split health deduction totals the same as the joint one. Symmetric incomes in the same bracket => the divide-by-2/multiply-by-2 mechanism reproduces two individual assessments exactly (at most a 1-cent rounding artifact when a boundary is crossed).
